T1: Home ice maker demand is driven by convenience and the desire for fresh, chewable ice, not by energy efficiency or compact size alone. Who benefits: Residential consumers seeking convenient, high-quality ice for beverages and food preparation.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers switch from commercial ice machines to countertop models because they want ice readily available at home, reducing the need to visit a store or wait for delivery.. How value is captured: Hoshizaki can capture value by offering premium-priced, differentiated countertop models with features like nugget ice and easy refilling, justifying higher margins.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay a premium for convenience and taste.; The convenience motive outweighs cost considerations for most buyers.; Hoshizaki can differentiate its products through design and functionality.. Predictions: In a test offering a premium-priced countertop ice maker, purchase intent will be higher than for a standard commercial-grade unit.; Surveyed buyers will cite convenience as the primary reason for choosing the product..

T2: Home ice maker demand is driven by energy efficiency and cost savings, not by convenience or taste. Who benefits: Energy-conscious residential consumers and households looking to reduce electricity bills.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers switch to energy-efficient countertop models because they perceive lower long-term costs and environmental benefits, even if convenience is secondary.. How value is captured: Hoshizaki can capture value by positioning its products as energy-efficient, offering rebates or incentives, and selling at premium prices justified by cost savings.. Assumptions: Energy costs are a significant factor for residential buyers.; Consumers are willing to pay more for energy-efficient appliances.; Regulatory or market incentives will support energy-efficient home appliances.. Predictions: In a test offering an energy-efficient countertop ice maker, purchase intent will be higher than for a standard commercial-grade unit.; Surveyed buyers will cite cost savings and energy efficiency as the primary reason for choosing the product..

Test "Convenience vs Energy Efficiency Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Condition A (convenience-focused) or Condition B (energy-efficient-focused). Both conditions present a countertop ice maker with identical features (e.g., nugget ice, easy refilling, compact design). Participants are asked to indicate their primary purchase reason (convenience vs cost savings) and to state a willingness-to-pay price.. Sample: 300 residential consumers recruited via an online panel, balanced across the two conditions (150 per condition).. Measure: Primary purchase reason (convenience vs cost savings) and maximum willingness-to-pay price.. Predictions: T1: Condition A will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness-to-pay prices than Condition B, because convenience is the primary driver.; T2: Condition B will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness-to-pay prices than Condition A, because energy efficiency is the primary driver.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between the two conditions is at least 10 percentage points and the condition with the higher intent is the one that also shows the higher willingness-to-pay price, we conclude that the respective theory is supported. If the difference is less than 10 percentage points, we conclude that neither theory is strongly supported and further testing is needed.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes convenience and premium features (e.g., nugget ice, easy refilling) rather than energy efficiency. Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes convenience and premium features (e.g., nugget ice, easy refilling) rather than energy efficiency. Use the proposed convenience vs energy efficiency messaging test to validate whether convenience drives purchase intent and willingness to pay. If the test shows a meaningful advantage for convenience-focused messaging, proceed with a premium-priced counter Target customer: Residential consumers seeking convenient, high-quality ice for beverages and food preparation.. Value proposition: A premium-priced countertop ice maker that delivers fresh, chewable nugget ice with easy refilling, leveraging Hoshizaki’s design expertise and brand reputation to justify higher margins.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the 12‑week, €20,000 convenience vs energy efficiency messaging test with 300 residential consumers, analyzing purchase intent and willingness to pay by condition.. Uncertainty: The actual demand for a differentiated consumer proposition is unknown; the test will determine whether convenience or energy efficiency drives purchase decisions. Additionally, the willingness to pay for premium features remains uncertain.. sources.excerpt: DANBURY, Conn. — Belimo Americas, a manufacturer of damper actuators and control valves for commercial HVAC, announced the availability of products for residential applications with select actuators, round damper assemblies, and pressure bypass damper controls.

Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

Gross profit grew year-on-year in the Business and Pro segments, while gross profit in the Consumer segment was impacted negatively by a weakening US consumer sentiment, US tariffs and costs related to promotions and campaigns with key retail partners.

Belimo is a global market leader in the development, production, and sales of field devices for the energy-efficient control of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems. The focus of its core business is on damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters.

With an emphasis on product quality, durability with minimal maintenance, and highly innovative, technically advanced solutions, the Company has become a preferred choice in high-performance applications in large commercial buildings such as data centers, hospitals, schools and universities, offices, governmental buildings, infrastructure and industrial sites.

Belimo collaborates closely with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of HVAC systems and system integrators who incorporate Belimo products into large-scale HVAC projects. It provides them with extensive technical support, including planning, customization, calibration, and troubleshooting – and conducts training for HVAC professionals to optimize installation effectiveness.
In addition to our growing portfolio of DIY solutions sold through top retail and e-commerce channels, the majority of our technologies are installed by professionals.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Belimo Holding AG investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current HVAC actuators, valves, and sensors, sold to commercial building manufacturers and through controls contractors and system integrators.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Evidence must demonstrate consumer demand, willingness to pay, or a viable route to market for a differentiated consumer proposition.; Any recommendation must consider Belimo’s existing B2B business model and current reach to individual buyers.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., residential home automation, DIY HVAC control, or a new consumer segment).; 2) Expand the existing B2B product portfolio with new features or packaging without targeting consumers directly.; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on commercial building manufacturers and system integrators.; 4) Change the route to market (e.g., direct-to-consumer e‑commerce, partnerships with home‑im improvement retailers, or a subscription model for home control services).; 5) Target a different customer group within the commercial segment (e.g., small‑to‑medium office buildings, residential building owners, or energy‑efficient retrofits)..

T1: Consumers will adopt Belimo residential products if they perceive them as reliable, energy‑efficient, and easy to install, because they value performance and lower long‑term costs. Who benefits: Homeowners seeking efficient HVAC control and DIYers who prefer plug‑and‑play solutions.. Why behaviour changes: Growing awareness of energy savings and the availability of zone‑based residential control make consumers willing to choose Belimo over generic or competitor products.. How value is captured: Belimo can capture value by pricing premium on quality, durability, and support, and by selling through retail and e‑commerce channels at higher margins.. Assumptions: Consumers currently purchase HVAC control products primarily through professionals or large‑scale OEMs.; Belimo can communicate its technical advantages to individual buyers.; Retail/online channels will stock and promote Belimo residential products effectively.. Predictions: In a test offering a residential zone damper at a retail price, at least 20% of respondents will express intent to purchase or purchase within 12 weeks.; Surveyed homeowners will rank Belimo higher for energy efficiency and durability compared to competitors when presented with product specifications..

T2: Consumers will adopt Belimo residential products if they perceive them as a status or brand signal, because they value prestige and the association with a trusted, high‑performance HVAC brand. Who benefits: Affluent homeowners and early adopters who seek to signal sophistication and reliability in their home automation choices.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers increasingly view products as a reflection of personal taste and lifestyle, and Belimo’s reputation for technical excellence and durability makes it an attractive premium choice.. How value is captured: Belimo can capture value by positioning its residential products as a premium, brand‑driven offering, allowing higher price points and limited edition designs, and by leveraging its existing OEM relationships to reach niche markets.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay a premium for brand prestige in home automation.; Belimo’s brand perception can be effectively communicated to individual buyers.; A limited‑edition or exclusive product line can generate demand without overwhelming production capacity.. Predictions: In a test offering a limited‑edition residential zone damper at a premium price, at least 15% of respondents will express intent to purchase or purchase within 12 weeks.; Surveyed homeowners will rank Belimo higher for brand prestige and status compared to competitors when presented with product features..

Test "Residential Zone Damper Purchase Intent Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase offer and product description. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Condition A (T1) receives a product description emphasizing energy efficiency, durability, and ease of installation; Condition B (T2) receives a product description emphasizing brand prestige, status, and limited edition design. Both conditions include a simulated purchase offer at a fixed retail price.. Sample: 500 U.S. homeowners aged 25-55 who have considered purchasing a residential HVAC control product in the past 12 months, recruited via an online panel.. Measure: Purchase intent measured as the percentage of respondents who indicate they would purchase the product within 12 weeks, and willingness to pay (WTP) in a 7-point scale.. Predictions: T1: Condition A will generate purchase intent at least 20% higher than Condition B, and WTP will be at least 10% higher for the energy‑efficiency‑focused description.; T2: Condition B will generate purchase intent at least 20% higher than Condition A, and WTP will be at least 10% higher for the prestige‑focused description.. Decision rule: If Condition A purchase intent is at least 20% higher than Condition B, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition focused on energy efficiency and ease of installation (support T1). If Condition B purchase intent is at least 20% higher than Condition A, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition focused on brand prestige and limited edition design (support T2). If neither condition meets the 20% threshold, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition and continue focusing on B2B OEMs and integrators.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

T1: Consumers will adopt differentiated protective gloves for specific use cases (e.g., outdoor recreation, cycling, gardening) if they perceive the product as a premium, specialized item that offers superior protection and style, leading to higher purchase frequency and willingness to pay a premium price. Who benefits: Outdoor enthusiasts, cyclists, gardeners, and consumers seeking specialized protection who currently rely on generic or generic-like gloves.. Why behaviour changes: Shifting from generic gloves to specialized gloves creates a perceived value difference, making consumers willing to switch from one brand to another for the specific use case.. How value is captured: Ansell can capture value by pricing differentiated products at premium levels, leveraging its brand reputation for industrial and healthcare protection, and selling through specialized retail channels or direct-to-consumer platforms.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay a premium for specialized protection.; Specialized gloves offer measurable performance advantages over generic gloves.; Ansell can effectively communicate the specialized benefits to consumers.. Predictions: In a test offering a differentiated outdoor glove at a premium price, purchase intent will be higher than for a generic glove at the same price point.; Surveyed consumers will rank the specialized feature as the primary reason for choosing the product..

T2: Consumers will adopt differentiated protective gloves for specific use cases if they perceive the product as a lifestyle accessory that aligns with their personal brand or identity, leading to higher purchase frequency and brand loyalty. Who benefits: Consumers who value personal branding and identity in their purchasing decisions, such as outdoor enthusiasts, fitness enthusiasts, and lifestyle buyers.. Why behaviour changes: When consumers view protective gloves as a fashion or lifestyle item rather than just a functional product, they are more likely to purchase multiple pairs and remain loyal to the brand.. How value is captured: Ansell can capture value by creating lifestyle-branded products, offering limited editions, and selling through premium retail channels that emphasize personal style and identity.. Assumptions: Consumers associate protective gloves with personal branding.; Lifestyle branding increases perceived value beyond functional protection.; Ansell can effectively brand gloves as lifestyle items without compromising protection.. Predictions: In a test offering a lifestyle-branded glove, purchase intent will be higher than for a functional-branded glove of similar price.; Consumers will report higher brand loyalty and willingness to recommend the product to peers..

Test "Premium vs Eco Positioning Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized exposure to two product descriptions of a Franke consumer machine. Participants are randomly assigned to view either a premium positioning description (emphasizing professional quality, convenience, and modern design) or an eco‑friendly positioning description (emphasizing sustainability, water‑conserving features, and eco‑certification). After viewing the description, participants indicate purchase intent on a 7‑point scale (1‑not interested to 7‑very interested) and state their top reason for choosing the machine.. Sample: 300 adult consumers in Germany and Switzerland, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income to ensure representativeness.. Measure: Purchase intent score (7‑point scale) and top reason for choosing the machine.. Predictions: T1: Participants exposed to the premium positioning description will report higher purchase intent and will cite taste and convenience as their top reason.; T2: Participants exposed to the eco‑friendly positioning description will report higher purchase intent and will cite sustainability as their top reason.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent score for the premium positioning group is at least 1.5 points higher than for the eco‑friendly positioning group, and the difference is statistically significant (p < 0.05), then T1 is supported. If the difference is not statistically significant, the test is inconclusive, and further evidence is needed.. Cost: 15000 euros, 8 weeks.

Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

Test "Consumer Messaging Test for Dräger Home Safety Devices" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are recruited from German and Austrian households (n=500). They are randomly assigned to one of three message conditions: (1) Trusted professional brand (Dräger police/medical reputation); (2) Regulatory compliance (CO alarms, breathalyzers required by law); (3) Neutral control. Participants indicate purchase intent (1‑10) and maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 500 German and Austrian homeowners/renters (250 per condition) to ensure regional diversity.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and maximum price willingness to pay for each condition.. Predictions: T1: Condition 1 (professional brand) will achieve the highest purchase intent and highest price willingness compared to Condition 2 and Control.; T2: Condition 2 (regulatory compliance) will achieve the highest purchase intent and highest price willingness compared to Condition 1 and Control.. Decision rule: If Condition 1 purchase intent ≥ 40% and Condition 2 purchase intent ≤ 30%, proceed to develop a consumer proposition emphasizing professional brand trust. If Condition 2 purchase intent ≥ 40% and Condition 1 purchase intent ≤ 30%, proceed to develop a consumer proposition emphasizing regulatory compliance. If neither condition meets its threshold, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Test "Premium vs. Design Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Premium Group (hygiene and convenience messaging) or Design Group (design and space-saving messaging). Both groups see a product description of a Winterhalter undercounter dishwasher with four sizes (S, M, L, XL). The Premium Group also sees a price premium of 20% over a standard model; the Design Group also sees a price premium of 15% over a standard model. Participants indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 300 adult homeowners (150 per group) recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and household income.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and maximum price willingness to pay (EUR).. Predictions: T1: Premium Group will have higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than Design Group.; T2: Design Group will have higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than Premium Group.. Decision rule: If Premium Group average purchase intent ≥ 7.5 and Design Group average purchase intent ≤ 6.5, proceed with premium, hygiene-focused consumer proposition. If Design Group average purchase intent ≥ 7.5 and Premium Group average purchase intent ≤ 6.5, proceed with design, space‑saving consumer proposition. If neither threshold is met, do not expand.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., home kitchen dishwashers) with premium, hygiene and convenience messaging. Use the proposed Premium vs. Design Messaging Test to validate consumer demand before committing to full development. If the test shows purchase intent above 7.5 for the Premium Group, proceed with a premium, feature-rich model; otherwise, reconsider the investment. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: DANBURY, Conn. — Belimo Americas, a manufacturer of damper actuators and control valves for commercial HVAC, announced the availability of products for residential applications with select actuators, round damper assemblies, and pressure bypass damper controls.

Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

Gross profit grew year-on-year in the Business and Pro segments, while gross profit in the Consumer segment was impacted negatively by a weakening US consumer sentiment, US tariffs and costs related to promotions and campaigns with key retail partners.

Belimo is a global market leader in the development, production, and sales of field devices for the energy-efficient control of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems. The focus of its core business is on damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters.

With an emphasis on product quality, durability with minimal maintenance, and highly innovative, technically advanced solutions, the Company has become a preferred choice in high-performance applications in large commercial buildings such as data centers, hospitals, schools and universities, offices, governmental buildings, infrastructure and industrial sites.

Belimo collaborates closely with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of HVAC systems and system integrators who incorporate Belimo products into large-scale HVAC projects. It provides them with extensive technical support, including planning, customization, calibration, and troubleshooting – and conducts training for HVAC professionals to optimize installation effectiveness.
The company’s first product launch of 2020 offers HVAC contractors reliable, high-quality solutions with precise performance and offers the value-conscious homeowner a wider range of options.
In addition to our growing portfolio of DIY solutions sold through top retail and e-commerce channels, the majority of our technologies are installed by professionals.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Belimo Holding AG investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current HVAC actuators, valves, and sensors, sold to commercial building manufacturers and through controls contractors and system integrators.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Evidence must demonstrate consumer demand, willingness to pay, or a viable route to market for a differentiated consumer proposition.; Any recommendation must consider Belimo’s existing B2B business model and current reach to individual buyers.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., residential home automation, DIY HVAC control, or a new consumer segment).; 2) Expand the existing B2B product portfolio with new features or packaging without targeting consumers directly.; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on commercial building manufacturers and system integrators.; 4) Change the route to market (e.g., direct-to-consumer e‑commerce, partnerships with home‑im improvement retailers, or a subscription model for home control services).; 5) Target a different customer group within the commercial segment (e.g., small‑to‑medium office buildings, residential building owners, or energy‑efficient retrofits)..

T1: Homeowners will adopt Belimo residential HVAC control products if they perceive them as a premium, energy‑efficient upgrade that reduces long‑term costs, because they value comfort and lower utility bills. Who benefits: Belimo gains higher margins and brand prestige by selling premium products directly to consumers.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers shift from generic thermostats to Belimo when they understand the product offers superior energy‑efficiency and lower operating costs over time.. How value is captured: Belimo captures value through direct‑to‑consumer sales at premium prices, bypassing OEM margins and retail intermediaries.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay a premium for energy‑efficient HVAC control.; Belimo can communicate the cost‑savings benefit effectively to homeowners.; The market size for residential HVAC control is large enough to support a differentiated consumer proposition.. Predictions: In a test offering a Belimo residential thermostat at a 20% premium over a generic equivalent, purchase intent will be at least 15% higher than for a generic thermostat.; Surveyed homeowners will cite energy‑efficiency and long‑term cost savings as primary reasons for choosing Belimo..

T2: Homeowners will adopt Belimo residential HVAC control products because they trust the brand from commercial building manufacturers and seek reliability and compatibility with existing HVAC systems, leading to repeat purchases and service loyalty. Who benefits: Belimo gains repeat revenue and brand extension by selling to homeowners through OEM channels, leveraging its commercial reputation.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers choose Belimo when they perceive it as a trusted, professional-grade product that integrates seamlessly with their existing HVAC systems, reducing installation and maintenance concerns.. How value is captured: Belimo captures value through OEM partnerships and direct-to-consumer sales at standard prices, using its commercial brand to justify premium pricing.. Assumptions: Consumers prioritize brand trust and compatibility over price.; Belimo's commercial reputation transfers to residential products.; OEM channels can effectively reach homeowners.. Predictions: In a test offering a Belimo residential thermostat through a home improvement retailer, purchase intent will be at least 10% higher than for a generic equivalent sold directly.; Homeowners will cite compatibility with existing HVAC systems as the primary reason for choosing Belimo..

events.text: Objective: Determine whether Testo SE & Co. KGaA should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current B2B portable and stationary measuring instruments, based on evidence of market demand, competitive positioning, and feasibility within budget and time constraints.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Current consumer reach is unknown; must be discovered from public sources.; Any new proposition must be justified by evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and competitive advantage.; Investment decision must consider risk, resource allocation, and potential impact on existing B2B operations.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home DIY, small business, or consumer health monitoring) with a new product or service model.; 2) Expand the existing B2B product line into adjacent consumer segments without a differentiated proposition (e.g., add consumer‑focused accessories or services).; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on the current B2B market and existing product portfolio.; 4) Change the route to market for existing B2B products to reach consumers directly (e.g., e‑commerce, subscription services) without altering the core product.; 5) Target a different customer group within the B2B segment (e.g., small trades, individual contractors) with a differentiated proposition..

T1: Homeowners will adopt Testo's portable measuring instruments for energy efficiency auditing because they need to verify insulation, gas/fuel heating, or air quality to reduce heating bills, and Testo offers a trusted, accurate reading tool that consumers trust more than DIY apps or self‑reading. Who benefits: Homeowners with low‑income heating bills who cannot afford professional audits and need credible data to justify upgrades.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers adopt Testo when they perceive the device as an authoritative, easy‑to‑use tool that provides measurable results, reducing uncertainty and cost of decision‑making.. How value is captured: Testo captures value through higher‑margin direct‑to‑consumer sales of portable devices and potential subscription services for data analysis or certification.. Assumptions: Consumers currently rely on manual checks or apps that are unreliable.; Price sensitivity for energy‑efficiency tools is lower than for premium consumer electronics.; Regulatory or incentive mechanisms (e.g., green buildings) create demand for verification.. Predictions: A survey of homeowners showing >40% would purchase a Testo portable device if priced under €100 will generate demand.; Sales of the same device in consumer channels will exceed sales in B2B channels when marketed to individual homeowners..

T2: Homeowners will adopt Testo's portable measuring instruments for home energy efficiency auditing because they are concerned about rising heating costs and want to reduce their carbon footprint, and Testo offers a trusted, accurate tool that aligns with their sustainability goals. Who benefits: Environmentally conscious homeowners who are motivated by cost savings and want to contribute to carbon reduction.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers adopt Testo when they perceive the device as a credible, easy-to-use tool that provides measurable results, making energy‑efficiency upgrades feel achievable and rewarding.. How value is captured: Testo captures value through premium pricing for consumer‑focused devices and potential partnerships with sustainability‑focused retailers or eco‑friendly initiatives.. Assumptions: Energy‑efficiency upgrades are a growing consumer priority.; Consumers are willing to pay a premium for accuracy and trust.; Sustainability messaging can drive purchase decisions.. Predictions: A survey showing >30% of homeowners would purchase a Testo device if priced at €120+ will indicate demand.; Sales in consumer channels will be higher than in B2B channels when marketed on sustainability benefits..

Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A sees a premium positioning message emphasizing Swiss engineering and superior taste; Group B sees a convenience positioning message emphasizing integrated grinding and brewing. Both groups see the same product description (Franke A300 Fresh Brew). Participants indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10) and state maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 400 adult consumers in Germany and Switzerland, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and maximum price willingness to pay.. Predictions: T1: Group A will have a higher average purchase intent score and a higher average maximum price willingness to pay than Group B.; T2: Group B will have a higher average purchase intent score and a higher average maximum price willingness to pay than Group A.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent score for Group A is at least 1.5 points higher than Group B (i.e., Group A’s average ≥ 5.5), we conclude that premium positioning drives higher demand and justify investing in a differentiated consumer proposition. If Group B’s average is at least 1.5 points higher, we conclude convenience drives demand and recommend a convenience-focused approach. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, we conclude neither positioning is significantly superior and recommend no expansion.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Test "DIY Insulation Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are randomly assigned to one of three groups: Group A (government‑approved, SEAI One Stop Shop messaging), Group B (premium performance messaging), and Group C (neutral control). Each group views a product description of Kingspan insulation and is asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7‑point scale (1‑not likely to 7‑very likely).. Sample: 300 UK homeowners (150 per group) recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and region.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑to 7) for each group.. Predictions: T1: Group A will have the highest average purchase intent score (≈5.5) due to trust in government funding and the SEAI One Stop Shop process.; T2: Group B will have the highest average purchase intent score (≈5.5) due to premium performance messaging, even without government funding.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent score for Group A is at least 1.5 points higher than Group B, conclude T1 is supported. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, conclude T2 is supported. If neither difference is statistically significant, conclude neither theory is strongly supported.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

Once treated water leaves the plant, it can come in contact with various components within the distribution system that potentially alter the quality of the water before it reaches consumers. This makes it hard to guarantee quality for the customer and emphasizes the importance of testing samples in the field.

Drinking water test kits (home test kits) are widely available at hardware stores and the internet, allowing customers to independently assess their drinking water quality at their tap. These kits provide several tests, including: pesticides, bacteria, lead, copper, nitrate, nitrite, iron, chlorine, pH, hardness, and alkalinity.

Home test kit results should be considered an initial step, not a final result. A poor water quality result by a kit should be confirmed with follow-up analyses by a laboratory that uses state-of-the-art instruments, certified methods, and quality control measures to ensure accuracy and reliability.

Test "Digital Messaging Test: Public Funding vs Premium Positioning" between T1; T2. Method: Run a targeted online ad campaign with two versions: Version A presents Kingspan insulation as a government‑approved, SEAI‑backed solution for energy‑efficiency grants; Version B positions it as a premium, high‑performance product with superior thermal efficiency and durability. Both versions are shown to homeowners in the same geographic region with similar demographics.. Sample: 2,000 homeowners in the target region, recruited via an online panel, split evenly between Version A and Version B.. Measure: Conversion rate (percentage of visitors who click “Buy Now” or add to cart) and average willingness‑to‑pay (WTP) stated in a follow‑up survey.. Predictions: T1: Version A will achieve a higher conversion rate and WTP than Version B, because homeowners are motivated by public funding and grant compliance.; T2: Version B will achieve a higher conversion rate and WTP than Version A, because homeowners are willing to pay a premium for perceived superior performance.. Decision rule: If Version A’s conversion rate exceeds Version B’s by at least 5 percentage points and its WTP is at least €200 higher, conclude T1 is supported. If Version B’s conversion rate exceeds Version A’s by at least 5 percentage points and its WTP is at least €200 higher, conclude T2 is supported. If neither difference meets the 5‑point threshold, the test is inconclusive and further evidence is needed.. Cost: 15000 euros, 6 weeks.

Test "Consumer Preference Test for Home Ice Machine" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenario and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions.. Sample: 500 U.S. residential consumers (aged 18-55) recruited via an online panel, balanced for gender and geographic region.. Measure: 1) Purchase intent: "Would you purchase a home ice machine for personal use?" (binary: Yes/No). 2) WTP: "What is the maximum price you would pay for a home ice machine with a premium feature (e.g., nugget ice, unpasteurized ice, energy efficiency) compared to a standard commercial unit?" (price point). 3) Primary purchase driver: "Which of the following best describes why you would choose this ice machine?" (convenience, taste, health/wellness, other).. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and higher WTP for a differentiated home ice machine than for a standard commercial unit, with convenience and taste as top drivers.; T2: Higher purchase intent and higher WTP for a health-focused home ice machine than for a differentiated home ice machine, with health/wellness as top driver.. Decision rule: If the observed purchase intent for the differentiated home ice machine exceeds the standard commercial unit by at least 15 percentage points and the WTP is at least 20% higher than the standard unit, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition. If the difference is less than 15 points or the WTP difference is less than 20%, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and consider other alternatives.. Cost: 15000 euros, 6 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., home ice machine) based on evidence of consumer demand for convenience and the existence of a differentiated market segment. Conduct a small-scale test (e.g., purchase intent survey) to validate demand before committing to full development. If the test shows a meaningful advantage, proceed; otherwise, consider other alternatives. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., home ice machine) based on evidence of consumer demand for convenience and the existence of a differentiated market segment. Conduct a small-scale test (e.g., purchase intent survey) to validate demand before committing to full development. If the test shows a meaningful advantage, proceed; otherwise, consider other alternatives. Target customer: Residential consumers aged 18-55 who value convenience, fresh ice, and are willing to pay a premium for premium features.. Value proposition: A differentiated home ice machine that offers convenience, high-quality nugget ice, and energy efficiency, sold through retail channels at a premium price.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer Preference Test (500 U.S. residential consumers, 6 weeks, €15,000) to measure purchase intent and willingness to pay for a differentiated home ice machine versus a standard commercial unit.. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market, the willingness to pay for premium features, and the ability to reach individual buyers through retail channels are uncertain. The test will resolve these uncertainties.. Would change if: If the test shows purchase intent for the differentiated home ice machine is at least 15 percentage points lower than for a standard commercial unit, or if willingness to pay is at least 20% lower, we would reconsider the investment.; If new evidence shows strong consumer demand driven by health or unpasteurized ice, we would revise the theory and test a health-focused proposition.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

case.question: Should Laerdal Medical develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, beyond its existing resuscitation and healthcare-simulation training products? What evidence would justify that investment?

sources.excerpt: In 2010, bystanders administered CPR in 61 percent of public cases and 28.3 percent of in-home cases. In 2014, the rate of bystander CPR rose to 70.6 percent of public cases and 41.3 percent of in-home cases.
Today, more than 350,000 cardiac arrests occur outside of hospitals in the United States annually. Nearly three out of four of those cardiac arrests happen in homes.

Laerdal Medical is a global leader in healthcare education and resuscitation training, using advanced technology and data-driven insights to improve survival rates and enhance the quality of care. We empower our heroes and lifesavers – healthcare professionals – to help them save more lives.

CPR Anytime is a flexible program that allows you to learn CPR at your own pace, in the comfort and privacy of your home. The kits can also facilitate large CPR training programs in school, workplace, or community settings. The kit is portable, making it easy to share with family members or close friends – resulting in more people trained.

At a time marked by geopolitical instability, war in Europe, and growing demands for national preparedness, Laerdal is strengthening its focus on competence, learning, and collaboration in emergency medical services, both civilian and military.

LEBANON – The intensive care nursery (ICN) at Children’s Hospital at Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center (CHaD), New Hampshire’s only children’s hospital, recently received a donation of 500 Infant CPR Anytime kits from the American Heart Association (AHA), funded by the Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Foundation. The kits contain tools to help new parents learn the lifesaving skills of infant CPR and infant choking relief in as little as 20 minutes and are being distributed to families being discharged from the ICN.

T1: Consumers will adopt home CPR training if it is positioned as a safety and preparedness product for families, because they view CPR as a life-saving skill they should be able to perform in emergencies. Who benefits: Individual homeowners and their families who want to be prepared for cardiac emergencies.. Why behaviour changes: Growing public awareness of home cardiac arrests and the desire to be prepared for emergencies creates a perceived need for accessible, at-home training.. How value is captured: Laerdal can sell premium-priced home training kits directly to consumers, generate recurring revenue through optional add-ons (e.g., family training sessions), and build a brand of personal preparedness.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay for home CPR training if it is marketed as a safety product.; The market size for home CPR training is large enough to support a differentiated consumer proposition.; Laerdal can reach consumers through existing channels (e.g., online, retail) without significant new investment.. Predictions: If offered a home CPR training kit, a measured percentage of target homeowners will purchase it within 12 weeks.; Purchase intent will be higher among homeowners who report concern about home cardiac arrests compared to those who do not.; Repeat purchase or subscription rates will be higher for families who receive additional training resources..

T2: Consumers will adopt home CPR training if it is marketed as a health insurance or employer wellness benefit, because they view it as a cost-effective way to meet insurance or workplace requirements. Who benefits: Insurance companies, employers, and individual policyholders who need to meet coverage or wellness criteria.. Why behaviour changes: Insurance and employer mandates require employees or policyholders to complete CPR training, creating a demand for accessible, affordable home training that meets compliance.. How value is captured: Laerdal can sell training kits through insurance or HR channels, charge a premium for compliance-focused packaging, and generate recurring revenue from optional training extensions.. Assumptions: Insurance and employer requirements for CPR training exist and are enforceable.; Consumers are willing to purchase training kits as a compliance solution rather than a personal safety product.; Laerdal can partner with insurers or HR departments to reach target buyers.. Predictions: If offered a home CPR training kit as a compliance product, a measured percentage of target homeowners will purchase it within 12 weeks.; Purchase intent will be higher among homeowners who receive training through their insurance or workplace compared to those who purchase for personal reasons.; Repeat purchase rates will be higher for families who receive training as part of a compliance program..

Test "Home CPR Training Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Recruit 500 homeowners (300 per arm) who have a child under 18. Randomly assign participants to one of two messaging conditions: Condition A (personal safety) or Condition B (insurance/compliance). Both conditions present a home CPR training kit at a fixed price of €99. Track purchase intent (binary: "Would you buy this kit?") and willingness to pay (maximum amount).. Sample: 500 homeowners (300 per arm) recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, income, and home ownership.. Measure: Purchase intent rate (percentage of participants who say "Would you buy this kit?" is yes) and average willingness to pay (EUR).. Predictions: T1: Condition A will have a higher purchase intent rate than Condition B because the messaging emphasizes personal safety and preparedness.; T2: Condition B will have a higher purchase intent rate than Condition A because the messaging emphasizes insurance/compliance requirements.. Decision rule: If purchase intent in Condition A exceeds Condition B by at least 5 percentage points (e.g., 45% vs 40%), proceed to develop a consumer proposition focused on personal safety. If Condition B exceeds Condition A by at least 5 percentage points, pursue a compliance-focused proposition. If the difference is below 5 points, conduct further testing.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for home CPR training, focusing on personal safety and preparedness. Begin with a small-scale online survey test (e.g., X1) to validate purchase intent and willingness to pay before scaling. Use the results to decide whether to pursue a direct-to-consumer or partner-based approach. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for home CPR training, focusing on personal safety and preparedness. Begin with a small-scale online survey test (e.g., X1) to validate purchase intent and willingness to pay before scaling. Use the results to decide whether to pursue a direct-to-consumer or partner-based approach. Target customer: Individual homeowners and their families who want to be prepared for cardiac emergencies.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Home CPR Training Messaging Test (X1) to measure purchase intent and willingness to pay under personal safety messaging versus insurance/compliance messaging.. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market for home CPR training and the actual willingness to pay are unknown. The test will clarify whether consumers will purchase for personal safety or for compliance reasons.. Would change if: If the test shows purchase intent for the personal safety message is at least 5 percentage points higher than for the compliance message, we would proceed with a consumer proposition focused on personal safety.; If the test shows no significant difference or compliance messaging outperforms personal safety, we would reconsider the strategy and possibly explore a compliance-focused approach or partner with insurers/HR departments.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Consumer Preference Test: Convenience vs Safety Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Measure: Primary measure: average willingness-to-pay (WTP) for each condition. Secondary measure: purchase intent (likelihood to buy on a 7-point scale).. Test "Willingness-to-Pay Survey for Home Office vs Eco-Conscious Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are recruited from home office professionals and environmentally conscious consumers. Each participant sees one of two product descriptions: a home office-focused description emphasizing professional-grade coffee and workflow efficiency, and an eco-friendly description emphasizing sustainable materials, carbon-neutral production, and ethical sourcing. After viewing the description, participants indicate their maximum price they would pay for the machine.. Sample: 300 participants: 150 home office professionals (recruited via remote work forums) and 150 environmentally conscious consumers (recruited via sustainability-focused platforms).. Measure: Maximum price participants would pay for each product description.. Predictions: T1: Home office group will show a higher average willingness to pay for the home office description than for the eco description.; T2: Environmentally conscious group will show a higher average willingness to pay for the eco description than for the home office description.. Decision rule: If the average willingness to pay for the home office description exceeds the average willingness to pay for the eco description by at least 10% (e.g., home office average ≥ €150 and eco average ≤ €135), proceed to develop a differentiated home office proposition. If the opposite difference holds, proceed to develop an eco-friendly proposition. If the difference is within 5% (e.g., home office average ≥ €145 and eco average ≥ €140), consider both propositions and conduct a. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated home office proposition that emphasizes professional-grade coffee quality and workflow efficiency, supported by evidence of Franke's existing positioning for non-commercial spaces and the growing demand for home office coffee equipment. Conduct a willingness-to-pay survey to validate consumer price sensitivity before committing to full development. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated home office proposition that emphasizes professional-grade coffee quality and workflow efficiency, supported by Franke’s existing positioning for non‑commercial spaces and the growing demand for home office coffee equipment. Conduct a willingness‑to‑pay survey to validate consumer price sensitivity before committing to full development. Target customer: Home office professionals who need reliable, high‑quality coffee for remote work.. Value proposition: A premium, professional‑grade coffee machine designed for home office environments, offering consistent results and reduced preparation time, sold through Franke’s own brand.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed willingness‑to‑pay survey (or a smaller pilot) to measure price sensitivity and validate demand before full product development.. Uncertainty: The size of the home office market and actual willingness to pay for a differentiated machine are unknown; the survey results may not reflect real consumer behavior.. Would change if: If the survey shows a willingness to pay significantly below the proposed premium (e.g., <15% above baseline), the investment case weakens and a broader market proposition or licensing approach may be considered.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Consumer Proposition Preference Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging and purchase intent measurement.. Sample: 500 U.S. homeowners and small‑business owners (250 per arm) recruited via an online panel.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and willingness to pay (WTP) on a 7‑point scale.. Test "Consumer Preference Test: Convenience vs Brand Premium" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenarios. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups. Group A sees a description of a differentiated ice machine emphasizing convenience and novelty (e.g., nugget ice, easy refilling). Group B sees the same description but emphasizes brand ownership and premium quality (e.g., Scotsman brand, reliability). Both groups see a price point (e.g., €150) and a willingness-to-pay (WTP) question. After viewing the description, participants indicate their purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely) and state their maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 400 adult consumers in the United States, recruited via an online panel, balanced across both groups (200 per group).. Measure: Purchase intent score (1-7) and maximum price willingness to pay.. Predictions: T1: Group A will have a higher average purchase intent score and a higher average maximum price willingness to pay than Group B.; T2: Group B will have a higher average purchase intent score and a higher average maximum price willingness to pay than Group A.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent score for Group A is at least 1.5 points higher than Group B, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition focused on convenience and novelty (supporting T1). If Group B's average purchase intent score is at least 1.5 points higher than Group A, proceed to develop a branded premium proposition (supporting T2). If the difference is less than 1.5 points, indicate uncertainty and recommend further market research.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Test "Consumer Messaging Test for Home CPR Training" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are recruited from a panel of health-conscious consumers (n=500). Participants are randomly assigned to one of three groups: Group A (safety/peace-of-mind messaging), Group B (health/wellness routine messaging), and Group C (control group without messaging). Each group views a product description of a home CPR training kit and is asked to indicate willingness to pay (WTP) and likelihood to purchase on a 7-point scale.. Sample: 500 health-conscious consumers recruited from an online panel, balanced across age, gender, and geographic regions.. Measure: Average willingness to pay (WTP) and purchase intent (percentage of participants indicating they would purchase the kit) for each messaging group.. Predictions: T1: Group A will show the highest average WTP and purchase intent, as the safety/peace-of-mind message directly addresses life-saving motivation.; T2: Group B will show the highest average WTP and purchase intent, as the health/wellness routine messaging aligns with existing consumer health habits.. Decision rule: If Group A average WTP is at least 20 points higher than Group B and Group C, and the difference is statistically significant (p<0.05), proceed to develop a safety/peace-of-mind consumer proposition. If Group B average WTP is at least 20 points higher than Group A and Group C, and the difference is statistically significant, develop a health/wellness routine proposition. If neither group meets the 20-point threshold, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

Gross profit grew year-on-year in the Business and Pro segments, while gross profit in the Consumer segment was impacted negatively by a weakening US consumer sentiment, US tariffs and costs related to promotions and campaigns with key retail partners.

Belimo is a global market leader in the development, production, and sales of field devices for the energy-efficient control of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems. The focus of its core business is on damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters.

With an emphasis on product quality, durability with minimal maintenance, and highly innovative, technically advanced solutions, the Company has become a preferred choice in high-performance applications in large commercial buildings such as data centers, hospitals, schools and universities, offices, governmental buildings, infrastructure and industrial sites.

Belimo collaborates closely with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of HVAC systems and system integrators who incorporate Belimo products into large-scale HVAC projects. It provides them with extensive technical support, including planning, customization, calibration, and troubleshooting – and conducts training for HVAC professionals to optimize installation effectiveness.
In addition to our growing portfolio of DIY solutions sold through top retail and e-commerce channels, the majority of our technologies are installed by professionals.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Belimo Holding AG investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current HVAC actuators, valves, and sensors, sold to commercial building manufacturers and through controls contractors and system integrators.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Evidence must demonstrate consumer demand, willingness to pay, or a viable route to market for a differentiated consumer proposition.; Any recommendation must consider Belimo’s existing B2B business model and current reach to individual buyers.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., residential home automation, DIY HVAC control, or a new consumer segment).; 2) Expand the existing B2B product portfolio with new features or packaging without targeting consumers directly.; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on commercial building manufacturers and system integrators.; 4) Change the route to market (e.g., direct-to-consumer e‑commerce, partnerships with home‑im improvement retailers, or a subscription model for home control services).; 5) Target a different customer group within the commercial segment (e.g., small‑to‑medium office buildings, residential building owners, or energy‑efficient retrofits)..

T1: Homeowners will adopt Belimo residential HVAC controls primarily because they need reliable, lowMaintenance solutions for new energy-efficient homes, and they value compatibility with existing HVAC systems and integration with smart home platforms. Who benefits: Belimo gains a premium price and volume sales through OEMs and system integrators who bundle its products into new residential projects.. Why behaviour changes: Rising energy costs and government incentives make homeowners seek durable, controllable HVAC systems; Belimo's reputation for durability and technical support reduces perceived risk of high upfront cost.. How value is captured: Belimo captures value through high-margin OEM/ODM sales and recurring revenue from accessories, calibration, and service contracts.. Assumptions: Homeowners in new construction or major retrofits are willing to pay a premium for proven residential HVAC controls.; Compatibility with existing HVAC systems limits alternative options for homeowners.; Belimo can maintain its technical support and calibration services beyond the OEM relationship.. Predictions: In a survey, homeowners in new construction will indicate intent to purchase Belimo residential controls at a price 10-15% above generic alternatives.; Pilot sales of Belimo residential actuators through a select HVAC OEM will show higher conversion rates than generic alternatives.; Homeowners will report lower perceived maintenance frequency and higher satisfaction with Belimo products compared to generic residential controls..

T2: Homeowners will adopt Belimo residential HVAC controls because they value the brand’s reputation for reliability, technical precision, and compatibility with existing HVAC systems, and they are willing to pay a premium for proven performance in high‑performance buildings. Who benefits: Belimo gains premium pricing and volume sales through OEMs and system integrators who position its products as the go‑to choice for reliable residential HVAC control.. Why behaviour changes: Homeowners in new construction or major retrofits prioritize durability and technical accuracy over cost, and Belimo’s existing B2B reputation for high‑performance solutions transfers to residential buyers.. How value is captured: Belimo captures value through high‑margin OEM/ODM sales and recurring revenue from accessories, calibration, and service contracts that reinforce its technical credibility.. Assumptions: Homeowners in high‑performance residential projects (e.g., data centers, hospitals) already choose Belimo for its technical reputation.; The brand’s reputation for durability and precision is transferable to residential buyers despite higher price points.; Belimo can maintain its technical support and calibration services for residential customers beyond the OEM relationship.. Predictions: In a survey, homeowners in high‑performance residential projects will indicate intent to purchase Belimo residential controls at a price 15-20% above generic alternatives.; Pilot sales of Belimo residential actuators through a select HVAC OEM will show higher conversion rates among homeowners who already use Belimo’s products in commercial settings.; Homeowners will report higher satisfaction with Belimo products compared to generic residential controls, citing reliability and technical precision as primary reasons..

Test "Residential Control Preference Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenarios and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions.. Sample: 500 U.S. homeowners in new construction or major retrofits, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, income, and region.. Measure: 1) WTP for a Belimo residential HVAC control at a price 10-15% above generic alternatives. 2) Intent to purchase (binary: "Would buy"). 3) Primary reason for choosing Belimo (open-ended).. Predictions: T1: Homeowners will show WTP at least 10-15% above generic alternatives and higher intent to purchase than homeowners who already use Belimo’s commercial products.; T2: Homeowners will show WTP at least 15-20% above generic alternatives and higher intent to purchase than homeowners who already use Belimo’s commercial products.. Decision rule: If the average WTP for Belimo exceeds the generic baseline by ≥ 15% and is at least 10 points higher than the WTP for a generic alternative, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition. If the WTP difference is below 10 points or the generic baseline is met, do not invest in a consumer proposition.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Conduct the proposed Residential Control Preference Test (X1) to measure willingness-to-pay and purchase intent for a Belimo residential HVAC control at a 10-15% premium over generic alternatives. If the test meets the decision threshold (WTP ≥ 15% premium and ≥10-point difference from generic), proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition; otherwise, maintain the B2B focus and do not invest in a consumer Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: The simulated warehouse test (SYN-D) concerns a label printer reducing packing errors and does not address homeowner demand, willingness to pay, or purchase behavior for Belimo residential controls. Therefore it provides no evidence for or against T1, and the theory remains unchanged. New claim: Homeowners will adopt Belimo residential HVAC controls primarily because they need reliable, lowMaintenance solutions for new energy-efficient homes, and they value compatibility with existing HVAC systems and integration with smart home platforms.. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Do not commit to a consumer proposition yet. Conduct the proposed Residential Control Preference Test (X1) to measure willingness-to-pay and purchase intent for a Belimo residential HVAC control at a 10-15% premium over generic alternatives. If the test meets the decision threshold (WTP ≥ 15% premium and ≥10-point difference from generic), proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition; otherwise, maintain Target customer: Homeowners in new construction or major retrofits who seek reliable, lowMaintenance HVAC controls and are willing to pay a premium for proven residential solutions.. Value proposition: Belimo residential HVAC controls that combine durability, technical precision, and compatibility with existing HVAC systems, sold through OEMs and system integrators at a premium price, with recurring revenue from accessories, calibration,. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the Residential Control Preference Test (X1) within the 12‑week, €20,000 budget, and collect WTP and purchase intent data. Use the decision rule to decide whether to invest in a consumer proposition.. Uncertainty: Both T1 and T2 remain uncertain due to lack of direct evidence of homeowner demand, willingness to pay, and actual purchase behavior. The test will resolve this uncertainty.. Would change if: If the test shows WTP below 10% premium or no purchase intent, we would abandon the consumer proposition and focus on the B2B model.; If the test shows WTP above 15% premium and a ≥10-point difference from generic alternatives, we would proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition.; If new evidence from independent sources shows strong consumer demand or low price sensitivity, we would reconsider the investment case.. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether Ansell Limited should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current industrial and healthcare protective gloves and body protection, based on evidence of market demand, competitive landscape, and feasibility within budget and time constraints.. Constraints: Limited to public sources for evidence; internal financial or contractual details may not be public.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Current consumer reach to individual buyers is unknown and must be discovered.; Any recommendation must be justified by evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and competitive advantage.. Who benefits: Individual consumers who need reliable protection for activities where existing consumer gloves fail.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers will switch to a differentiated Ansell brand if they experience superior protection, durability, and comfort compared to standard consumer gloves.. How value is captured: Ansell can charge premium prices for the differentiated consumer line and capture value through direct‑to‑consumer sales and brand equity.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay more for protected gloves when performance is clear.; The differentiated features (e.g., material, design) are distinct enough from existing consumer gloves.; Distribution channels (e.g., specialty outdoor retailers) exist for the target use case.. Predictions: A test offering a differentiated outdoor‑recreation glove will generate higher conversion rates than an identical non‑differentiated glove.; Surveyed consumers will report higher satisfaction with the differentiated glove than with standard consumer gloves..

T2: Consumers will adopt Ansell protective gloves for specific use cases if they perceive the gloves as a status symbol or brand association, leading to purchase driven by perceived prestige rather than functional need. Why behaviour changes: Consumers will choose a differentiated Ansell glove when it signals professionalism, reliability, or alignment with a preferred lifestyle, even if the functional difference is minimal.. How value is captured: Ansell can price the consumer line at a premium and capture value through limited‑edition collaborations, brand licensing, and direct‑to‑consumer sales channels that emphasize prestige.. Assumptions: Brand perception of Ansell as a trusted industrial/healthcare protector transfers to consumer perception.; Consumers are willing to pay a premium for a brand they associate with quality and professionalism.; The target use case (e.g., cycling, gardening) has a segment of consumers who value status and are willing to pay for it.. Predictions: A test offering a differentiated glove with a prestige‑focused marketing campaign will achieve higher purchase intent than an identical glove without such messaging.; Surveyed consumers will rank Ansell higher for prestige than for functional protection when presented with a status‑focused proposition..

DANBURY, Conn. — Belimo Americas, a manufacturer of damper actuators and control valves for commercial HVAC, announced the availability of products for residential applications with select actuators, round damper assemblies, and pressure bypass damper controls.

Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

Gross profit grew year-on-year in the Business and Pro segments, while gross profit in the Consumer segment was impacted negatively by a weakening US consumer sentiment, US tariffs and costs related to promotions and campaigns with key retail partners.

Belimo is a global market leader in the development, production, and sales of field devices for the energy-efficient control of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems. The focus of its core business is on damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters.

With an emphasis on product quality, durability with minimal maintenance, and highly innovative, technically advanced solutions, the Company has become a preferred choice in high-performance applications in large commercial buildings such as data centers, hospitals, schools and universities, offices, governmental buildings, infrastructure and industrial sites.

Belimo collaborates closely with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of HVAC systems and system integrators who incorporate Belimo products into large-scale HVAC projects. It provides them with extensive technical support, including planning, customization, calibration, and troubleshooting – and conducts training for HVAC professionals to optimize installation effectiveness.
In addition to our growing portfolio of DIY solutions sold through top retail and e-commerce channels, the majority of our technologies are installed by professionals.

In 2010, bystanders administered CPR in 61 percent of public cases and 28.3 percent of in-home cases. In 2014, the rate of bystander CPR rose to 70.6 percent of public cases and 41.3 percent of in-home cases.
Today, more than 350,000 cardiac arrests occur outside of hospitals in the United States annually. Nearly three out of four of those cardiac arrests happen in homes.

Laerdal Medical is a global leader in healthcare education and resuscitation training, using advanced technology and data-driven insights to improve survival rates and enhance the quality of care. We empower our heroes and lifesavers – healthcare professionals – to help them save more lives.

CPR Anytime is a flexible program that allows you to learn CPR at your own pace, in the comfort and privacy of your home. The kits can also facilitate large CPR training programs in school, workplace, or community settings. The kit is portable, making it easy to share with family members or close friends – resulting in more people trained.

At a time marked by geopolitical instability, war in Europe, and growing demands for national preparedness, Laerdal is strengthening its focus on competence, learning, and collaboration in emergency medical services, both civilian and military.

LEBANON – The intensive care nursery (ICN) at Children’s Hospital at Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center (CHaD), New Hampshire’s only children’s hospital, recently received a donation of 500 Infant CPR Anytime kits from the American Heart Association (AHA), funded by the Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Foundation. The kits contain tools to help new parents learn the lifesaving skills of infant CPR and infant choking relief in as little as 20 minutes and are being distributed to families being discharged from the ICN.

Test "Consumer Messaging Test: DIY vs Eco‑friendly Insulation Kits" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a Kingspan insulation kit (same technical spec). In Condition A, the description emphasizes energy‑efficiency and comfort benefits. In Condition B, the description emphasizes eco‑friendly credentials and sustainability values. Participants are then asked: "Would you purchase this kit at the price shown?" (binary: Yes/No).. Sample: 300 UK homeowners (150 per condition) recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, income, and home ownership.. Measure: Purchase intent rate (Yes/No) and willingness to pay (EUR).. Predictions: T1: Condition A will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than Condition B.; T2: Condition B will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than Condition A.. Decision rule: If Condition A purchase intent ≥ 60% and Condition B purchase intent ≤ 40%, conclude T1 is supported. If Condition B purchase intent ≥ 60% and Condition A purchase intent ≤ 40%, conclude T2 is supported. If neither condition meets its threshold, the test is inconclusive and further evidence is needed.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

Laerdal Medical is a global leader in healthcare education and resuscitation training, using advanced technology and data-driven insights to improve survival rates and enhance the quality of care. We empower our heroes and lifesavers – healthcare professionals – to help them save more lives.

CPR Anytime is a flexible program that allows you to learn CPR at your own pace, in the comfort and privacy of your home. The kits can also facilitate large CPR training programs in school, workplace, or community settings. The kit is portable, making it easy to share with family members or close friends – resulting in more people trained.

At a time marked by geopolitical instability, war in Europe, and growing demands for national preparedness, Laerdal is strengthening its focus on competence, learning, and collaboration in emergency medical services, both civilian and military.

Test "Consumer Messaging Test for Home CPR Training" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants are recruited from a panel of health-conscious adults (n=500). Participants are randomly assigned to one of three conditions: (1) Personal Health Responsibility (PHR) condition: product described as a personal health responsibility to be learned at home; (2) Health Routine Condition: product described as part of a broader health routine and endorsed by trusted health authorities; (3) Control Condition: no product description. All participants are asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and willingness to pay a premium (EUR).. Sample: 500 health-conscious adults recruited from an online panel, balanced across the three conditions.. Measure: Purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and willingness to pay a premium (EUR) for each condition.. Predictions: T1: PHR condition will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than Health Routine and Control conditions.; T2: Health Routine condition will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than PHR and Control conditions.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent in the PHR condition is at least 10 points higher than the average purchase intent in the Health Routine condition, and the difference is statistically significant (p<0.05), then T1 is supported. If the average purchase intent in the Health Routine condition is at least 10 points higher than the average purchase intent in the PHR condition, and the difference is statistically significant (p<0.05), then T2 is supported. If neither difference is statistically significant, the test is inconclusive and no expansion is recommended.. Cost: 15000 euros, 6 weeks.

Participants are recruited from a panel of health-conscious adults (n=500). Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A sees a safety-focused home CPR message (e.g., "Be prepared to save a life with home CPR training.") and Group B sees a convenience-focused home CPR message (e.g., "Learn CPR in 20 minutes with our portable kit."). Sample: 500 health-conscious adults recruited from an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region.. Measure: Primary measure: average WTP (in euros) and purchase intent (on a 7-point scale). Secondary measure: share of participants indicating intent to purchase each message.. Predictions: T1: Participants viewing the premium machine will report purchase intent scores at least 20 points higher than those viewing the standard machine.; T2: Participants viewing the standard machine will report purchase intent scores at least 20 points higher than those viewing the premium machine.. Decision rule: If the difference in average purchase intent scores between the premium and standard groups is at least 20 points in favor of the premium machine, proceed with developing a differentiated consumer proposition targeting home office users. If the difference is at least 20 points in favor of the standard machine, do not pursue a differentiated proposition. If the difference is less than 20 points, conduct further market research to understand why the premium machine does not outperform the standard machine.. Cost: 15000 euros, 8 weeks.

Constraints: Limited to publicly available information; no internal company data.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Evidence must demonstrate consumer demand, willingness to pay, and a viable route to market for a differentiated product.; Any recommendation must consider the company’s existing B2B business and its current reach to individual buyers.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home safety, personal protective equipment for non‑medical users).; 2) Expand the existing B2B portfolio by adding new medical or safety technologies to existing customer segments (hospitals, industry, fire services, police).; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on current B2B markets without introducing a consumer proposition.; 4) Partner with or license Drägerwerk’s technology to third‑party consumer brands rather than selling under its own brand..
